title: China’s AI Acceleration
gist: Moonshot AI's Kimi model has triggered a fresh Washington panic over Chinese AI, but the real Chinese edge is distribution: open-weight models that are cheap enough to dominate developer adoption from Africa to U.S. startups, forcing the Trump administration to abandon a proposed ban. Elsewhere the brief covers an Iran-Oman Hormuz transit deal, Ukraine's air-defense shortfall, and a $275bn Trump-class battleship bill.

insights.claim: China's decisive AI advantage is not frontier model quality but distribution: most top Chinese models including Kimi and DeepSeek are open-weight, letting anyone download the data and code to build bespoke versions at far lower cost.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Model-layer pricing power erodes fastest where open weights are good enough; value migrates to inference infrastructure, distribution, and application layers rather than closed frontier labs.
insights.quote: But China’s bigger innovation may be in how Kimi, DeepSeek, and its other models are taking over the market.
insights.locator: The prevailing wisdom indicates a U.S. lead

insights.claim: Moonshot AI's Kimi released a new version in July 2026 showing capabilities that potentially rival top U.S. models, which is what set off the latest round of Washington soul-searching over the AI race.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: The capability gap narrative is being re-tested roughly annually; each Chinese release compresses the perceived U.S. lead and pressures U.S. model pricing.
insights.quote: The latest round of soul-searching has been sparked by a model named Kimi that was created by Chinese company Moonshot AI.
insights.locator: The China Challenge

insights.claim: Cheap Chinese open-weight models give countries an easier on-ramp to AI than the expensive and increasingly unreliable American tech stack Washington is trying to export.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: U.S. AI-stack export diplomacy is losing on both price and reliability; expect eroding U.S. share of emerging-market AI infrastructure.
insights.quote: it’s a form of Chinese AI-maxxing that gives countries around the world an easier entry point into an AI ecosystem than the far more expensive (and increasingly unreliable) tech stack that Washington is exporting
insights.locator: As Rishi wrote soon after Kimi’s new model launched

insights.claim: Developers across Kenya, Uganda, Ghana, and Nigeria are increasingly choosing Chinese AI models over U.S. ones for business, legal, and education applications.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: African developer mindshare is an early indicator of long-run platform lock-in; the same dynamic that decided mobile OS share is now running in AI.
insights.quote: developers across Kenya, Uganda, Ghana, and Nigeria are increasingly opting for Chinese AI models over U.S. ones to build everything from business and legal tools to education applications
insights.locator: The choices that countries in Africa are making

themes.theme: U.S. policy cornered by its own dependence

insights.claim: U.S. startups are themselves largely hooked on Chinese open-weight models, which is why the Trump administration's internal debate over banning them ended quickly.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Domestic dependence is the binding constraint on AI export controls; bans on open models are structurally unlikely regardless of hawkish rhetoric.
insights.quote: Even U.S. startups are largely hooked on Chinese open-weight models, which resulted in a rather quick end to the Trump administration’s debate over whether they should be banned.
insights.locator: Even U.S. startups are largely hooked

insights.claim: Trump is reportedly set to exclude open models from an upcoming AI governance framework that would subject U.S. models to government review — meaning U.S. closed labs face regulatory burden that Chinese-dominated open models escape.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: A regulatory asymmetry that penalizes U.S. frontier labs relative to open-weight competitors; watch the framework's final text for compliance-cost exposure.
insights.quote: Trump is reportedly set to exclude open models from an upcoming AI governance framework that could subject U.S. models to government review
insights.locator: Even U.S. startups are largely hooked

insights.claim: Washington's actual policy response has been peripheral rather than structural: an import ban on new Chinese humanoid robots and a possible ban on some Chinese components in U.S. data centers.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Component-level bans create supply-chain cost and sourcing risk for U.S. data center build-outs without addressing the model-diffusion problem.
insights.quote: the administration appears to be tinkering around the edges, with an import ban last week on new Chinese humanoid robots and a possible ban on the use of some Chinese components in U.S. data centers
insights.locator: Meanwhile, the administration appears to be tinkering

insights.claim: Beijing has retaliated against the recent flurry of U.S. regulatory moves with its own export restrictions on technologies such as drones, ahead of Xi Jinping's anticipated September trip to meet Trump.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Drone export restrictions hit Western defense and commercial UAV supply chains; the September summit is a scheduled catalyst for either escalation or de-escalation.
insights.quote: Beijing has retaliated with its own set of export restrictions on technologies such as drones
insights.locator: Those are among a flurry of anti-China moves

insights.claim: Graham Allison argues China's AI strategy is a repeat of its established playbook — offer a product almost as good as the alternative at a far lower price — already proven in solar panels, fast trains, 5G, consumer electronics, and electric cars.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: If AI follows the solar/5G/EV template, expect margin collapse in commoditized model serving and Chinese share gains outside the U.S. regulatory perimeter.
insights.quote: China begins by offering a product almost as good as the alternative but at a far more affordable price.
insights.locator: Table stakes.

insights.claim: The Apple-vs-Android analogy is the operative one for AI platform outcomes: Android runs 70 percent of the world's smartphones and offers twice as many apps as iOS despite iOS's closed premium ecosystem.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Open ecosystems win volume share even when the closed one wins quality perception — a direct read-across to closed U.S. labs vs. Chinese open weights.
insights.quote: Android is used in 70 percent of smartphones in the world and offers twice as many apps as Apple’s iOS
insights.locator: His chosen analogy is one that will be familiar

insights.claim: The United States is spending trillions of dollars on more advanced chips, more capable models, and new data centers to hold its AI lead, while China does more with less at a minuscule fraction of the cost.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: The U.S. capex-per-unit-of-capability disadvantage is the core bear case on AI infrastructure returns.
insights.quote: The fact that the United States’ only credible competitor in AI—China—is taking such a strikingly different path should make Americans pause and think,
insights.locator: Table stakes.

insights.claim: The disproportionate role AI investment now plays in the overall U.S. economy means a bursting AI bubble would carry catastrophic consequences for both the global economy and U.S. national security.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Explicitly frames AI capex as a systemic macro risk, not just a sector risk — relevant to index concentration and to any drawdown scenario analysis.
insights.quote: prompts Allison to warn (as many have) of a bubble whose bursting would have catastrophic consequences for the global economy and U.S. national security
insights.locator: Even without worrying about the rest of the world

insights.claim: Iran and Oman are close to a deal for commercial ships to transit the Strait of Hormuz under which Iran controls entry into the Persian Gulf and Oman controls the exit — and Iran says the United States is not a party to it.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: A Hormuz reopening without U.S. participation reprices tanker rates and crude risk premia while leaving Iran with structural chokepoint leverage.
insights.quote: Under the reported terms of the deal—which Iran said the United States is not a part of—Iran would control the passageway to enter the Persian Gulf through the strait, while Oman would control the exit.
insights.locator: Once MOUre.

insights.claim: The Iran-Oman transit arrangement is arriving nearly two months after a U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding pledged to reopen the waterway, indicating the U.S.-brokered track failed to deliver on its own.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: U.S. diplomatic follow-through on Iran is slow and substitutable; regional bilateral deals set the actual terms of trade through the chokepoint.
insights.quote: nearly two months after a memorandum of understanding between the United States and Iran pledged to open the crucial waterway
insights.locator: Once MOUre.

insights.claim: Trump publicly denied reports that the U.S. military has depleted nearly all of its long-range missiles in the Iran war, offering no specifics and threatening long-term jail sentences for those who leaked the stockpile news.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: If munitions depletion is real, U.S. escalation capacity against Iran is constrained and defense-primes' replenishment orders should follow.
insights.quote: The U.S. has massive amounts of ‘munitions,’ especially of certain types,
insights.locator: Trump, meanwhile, took to Truth Social

insights.claim: Israel rejected the U.S.-backed Hamas disarmament framework just days after Trump lauded it as a historic agreement.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Announcement-to-implementation slippage is the recurring pattern in this administration's Middle East deals; discount headline agreements accordingly.
insights.quote: Just days after Trump lauded a “historic” agreement for Hamas to disarm, Israel rejected the proposed framework this week.
insights.locator: Hamas disarmament.

insights.claim: Russia's missile and drone barrage on Kyiv killed at least 17 people and wounded more than 40, prompting Ukraine to strike two oil refineries hundreds of miles inside Russian territory.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Deep strikes on Russian refining capacity are a live supply-side risk to Russian crude product exports and to global diesel cracks.
insights.quote: Ukraine struck two oil refineries located hundreds of miles within Russian territory
insights.locator: Air defense gap.

insights.claim: Washington has stopped donating Patriot air defense missiles to Ukraine, and Trump pledged then swiftly backtracked on sharing the underlying Patriot technology with Kyiv.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: A structural interceptor shortfall for Ukraine raises escalation and casualty risk and shifts demand toward European air-defense suppliers.
insights.quote: Trump recently pledged to share the technology underpinning the powerful missile system with Kyiv before swiftly backtracking on the promise
insights.locator: The onslaught of Russian attacks has spotlighted

insights.claim: Zelensky is publicly arguing that partner delays in supplying anti-ballistic interceptors translate directly into civilian deaths, escalating the political pressure on Western capitals.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Public attribution of casualties to allied supply delays is a lever to force decisions; watch for a reversal on interceptor transfers.
insights.quote: It is very important that our partners understand that delays in supplying them, or an unwillingness to provide anti-ballistic systems, lead directly to such horrific casualties and destruction.
insights.locator: Zelensky, for his part, has continued to sound the alarm

insights.claim: The Congressional Budget Office puts the total expected cost of the U.S. Navy's new “Trump-class” battleship fleet at $275 billion.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: A $275bn program is a multi-decade revenue pool for naval shipbuilders and a crowding-out risk for other procurement lines.
insights.quote: $275 billion—the total expected cost of the U.S. Navy’s new “Trump-class” battleship fleet, according to a report by the Congressional Budget Office.
insights.locator: By the Numbers

insights.claim: FBI director Kash Patel says the agency has begun conducting joint operations with Russia and China, described here as U.S. adversaries.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: Operational law-enforcement cooperation with named adversaries is a material shift in U.S. security posture worth tracking for sanctions and enforcement implications.
insights.quote: FBI director Kash Patel telling Reuters that the agency has started conducting joint operations with U.S. adversaries Russia and China
insights.locator: Let’s Get Personnel

insights.claim: Todd Blanche's confirmation as attorney general remains uncertain despite advancing out of the Senate Judiciary Committee, because of pushback on his nomination and the GOP's razor-thin Senate majority.
insights.speaker: Rishi Iyengar, John Haltiwanger
insights.so_what: A razor-thin Senate majority is the operative constraint on this administration's personnel and legislative throughput.
insights.quote: his confirmation remains far from a sure thing given the pushback surrounding his nomination and the GOP’s razor-thin majority in the Senate
